origins: Habits and beliefs become comfortable over decades, and many hear “you can’t teach an old dog new tricks.” The result is resignation about patterns, health, relationships, or faith.
teaches: “Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind.” “Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation.” Paul said, “Though our outer self is wasting away, yet our inner self is being renewed day by day.” Caleb at 85 asked for a mountain (Joshua 14:10–12). Moses was 80 when God called him. Sarah and Abraham were old when God worked wonders. No one is too old for God to renew a heart or a habit.
self_statements: I have always been this way.
It is too late for me.
People my age do not change.
errors: Believing people either change when young or never.
Feeling set and concluding that I cannot.
questions: What change do I want most?
Have I ever changed something after age fifty or sixty?
Whom do I know who changed late in life?
What does Scripture say about God renewing us?
What is the smallest step I could take?
Who could support me in this change?
truth: Age does not limit God’s power to renew me. I can learn, grow, and change with small steps and His help.
hw_truths: My inner self is renewed daily.
I am a new creation in Christ.
log: Each week, note one thing you tried or learned.
actions: Choose a habit, belief, or skill.
Ask a friend to check in.
prayer: Lord, You renew me day by day. Give me courage to learn and change, and thank You that it is never too late. Amen.
